scope: Theorem 2.1 (Triangular increment) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are fixed D = Dk, η = ηk > 0, and polynomials with degrees depending only on k having the following property. Suppose p ≥ 2, a ≥ e−p, and a progression-free input on a positive-dimensional integer box has a certificate (2.2), with width logs Qh = log(2/wh). If every root side is sufficiently large with logarithmic cutoff polynomial in p, the dimension data, and all Qh, then either the hypotheses are impossible or a root slice carries a new certificate at threshold (1 + η)a. The new cell retains the determining data through exact integer reparametrizations and adds at most d0 = (2 + p)Ck fresh absolute slots together with downward preparation copies. Its dimensions d′ i and width logs Q′ i satisfy d′ i − di ≤ d0 + Pi(p, di+1, . . . , dD), (2.3) Q′ i − Qi ≤ P′ i (p, all dimension forecasts, Qi+1, . . . , QD). (2.4) The root slice cost has polynomial logarithmic bound in all the same data, now including every Qi. Polynomial exponents and the fixed gain are independent of the number of increments. Gap and discount choices can be made in advance from the dimension and cut-count forecasts.
